vulnerabilities.description: glob 10.2.0-10.4.5: Command injection via -c/--cmd executes matches with shell=true (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2). Used indirectly via @next/eslint-plugin-next. Allows arbitrary command execution during build.
vulnerabilities.impact: Build-time command injection could compromise development environment

vulnerabilities.description: Next.js 9.3.4-16.3.0: HTTP request smuggling in rewrites (GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8), Image Optimizer DoS (GHSA-9g9p-9gw9-jx7f), XSS in CSP nonces (GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q), Server Components DoS (GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3). Multiple critical DoS and security vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities.impact: Production exploitation possible: DoS, request smuggling, XSS via CSP nonces

vulnerabilities.description: PostCSS <8.5.10: XSS vulnerability via unescaped </style> in CSS stringify output (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93). Affects build-time CSS processing.
vulnerabilities.impact: Malicious CSS input during build could inject XSS into output pages

vulnerabilities.description: Weak random ID generation using Math.random().toString(36) instead of cryptographically secure random. IDs are predictable and could be enumerated.
vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers could predict or guess saved result IDs, potentially accessing or modifying other users' saved calculations

vulnerabilities.description: Session ID generated using Date.now() which is predictable. An attacker could enumerate valid session IDs based on time.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session ID prediction attacks; weak cryptographic randomness for session identifiers

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary file cleanup errors are silently ignored. If unlinkSync fails, sensitive GitHub content (API tokens, personal data) could remain on disk.
vulnerabilities.impact: Sensitive GitHub content persists on filesystem after command execution; disk forensics could recover data

vulnerabilities.description: Memory JSON file created with world-readable permissions (rw-rw-r--). If containing sensitive configuration or state, any user on system can read it.
vulnerabilities.impact: Horizontal privilege escalation on multi-user systems; stored secrets readable by other users

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary file created without explicit restrictive permissions. GitHub content (possibly containing tokens) accessible to other system users.
vulnerabilities.impact: Other users on shared systems could read sensitive GitHub content and credentials

vulnerabilities.description: Session JSON files created with default permissions (rw-rw-r--). Session context could contain sensitive information readable by other users.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session state, metrics, and context readable by other system users

vulnerabilities.description: Command execution logged to console showing file paths and command parameters. Sensitive GitHub content paths exposed in logs.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure: temporary file paths and potentially sensitive GitHub parameters logged to stdout

vulnerabilities.description: JSON parsing errors silently caught and ignored without logging. Corrupted memory.json files fail silently.
vulnerabilities.impact: Silent failures hide data corruption; state loss goes undetected; difficult debugging

vulnerabilities.description: JSON parsing errors in restore() are not caught. Invalid JSON crashes the operation.
vulnerabilities.impact: Corrupted session files cause unhandled exceptions and application crashes

vulnerabilities.description: File operations on security paths (.swarm/security) without path normalization. While unlikely, vulnerable to directory traversal attacks.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential directory traversal if paths are user-controlled in future versions

recommendations: CRITICAL (P0): Update Next.js to 16.2.6+ immediately to fix multiple DoS, XSS, and HTTP smuggling vulnerabilities
CRITICAL (P0): Update glob to 10.5.0+ or remove ESLint glob plugin to prevent command injection during builds
CRITICAL (P0): Update PostCSS to 8.5.10+ to fix XSS in CSS processing
CRITICAL (P0): Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() in src/lib/saved-results.ts line 22
HIGH (P1): Fix temporary file cleanup in .claude/helpers/github-safe.js - add retry logic and proper error handling
HIGH (P1): Replace Date.now() session ID with crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') in .claude/helpers/session.js line 15
HIGH (P1): Add try-catch blocks for all JSON.parse() operations in helper scripts
MEDIUM (P2): Set file permissions to 0o600 (owner-only) for all sensitive files: memory.js, session.js, and github-safe.js
MEDIUM (P2): Remove or sanitize console.log statements that expose file paths (line 80 in github-safe.js)
MEDIUM (P2): Add proper error logging instead of silent catches in memory.js load function
LOW (P3): Normalize and validate file paths in statusline.js using path.resolve()
Implement automated dependency scanning: run 'npm audit' in CI/CD pipeline
Review and document file permission requirements for all helper scripts

nextSteps.task: Run 'npm audit' and 'npm audit fix' to address dependency vulnerabilities
Update Next.js, glob, and PostCSS to patched versions
Fix cryptographic random ID generation in saved-results.ts
Fix file permissions and improve error handling in helper scripts

context.architecture: Frontend-only, no backend API or database
context.deployment: Static site generation with no server-side code execution
context.data_handling: Client-side only (localStorage) - no server-side data storage

notes: This codebase is primarily a static Next.js site with minimal backend exposure. The main security concerns are: (1) Dependency vulnerabilities in build-time and runtime dependencies, (2) Weak cryptography in client-side ID generation, (3) File permission issues in internal helper scripts for development workflows. No SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, or significant XSS vulnerabilities were found in the application code itself. The React components properly escape user content.
